subtitle.en: How El Niño / La Niña, the Indian Ocean Dipole and the Western-V steer Kenya's rains, harvests, food security and conflict — county by county.

intro.en: El Niño and La Niña are the ocean signals decision-makers act on. This notebook follows how that signal reaches each Kenyan county — through the Indian Ocean Dipole (short rains) and a partly-independent Western-V Pacific pattern (long rains) — and on to harvests, market prices, food insecurity and conflict. Pick a county to begin.

title.en: Where Do Things Stand Right Now?

insight.en: Kenya's rains are steered by ocean patterns — the **IOD** for the Oct–Dec short rains, a **Western-V** Pacific pattern for the Mar–May long rains. Pick a county and follow how the climate signal reaches its harvests, prices, food security and conflict.

mapHeading.en: Pick a county — Kenya at a glance

mapIntro.en: *Click any county to explore it through the story below; the selected county is outlined. Recolour the map to compare counties on what they grow, how green they are right now, food insecurity, or seasonal rainfall.*

mapCaption.en: Each county is shaded by the metric you choose. Value of production is the Atlas exposure snapshot (MapSPAM 2020 crops + GLW4 livestock, constant international dollars); NDVI and IPC are the latest available reading; rainfall is the long-term seasonal mean (CHIRPS). Click a county to make it the focus of every chart below; hover for its value. The colour scale rescales to the values on screen.

produceIntro.en: *What a county grows and herds, from the **KNBS National Agriculture Production Report** — the national statistics office's own subnational figures, collected by county officers across all 47 counties. Toggle **Crops** (production, 2019–2023) or **Livestock** (head of cattle/sheep/goats/camels/donkeys, 2021), pick a **view** (table / bars / treemap / trend), and switch to **% of national** for the county's share of Kenya's total. In the arid north and east, livestock dwarfs crops — which is why an ENSO drought that fails pasture hits those counties hardest.*

produceCaption.en: Source: **KNBS, National Agriculture Production Report 2023–2024** (Area & Production by County 2019–2023; livestock population by county 2021). Extracted by two independent PDF engines that must agree cell-by-cell, with each crop's county figures summing to the report's printed national total (additivity 100%) — no value read or typed by the model; each row keeps its source page. **% of national** = county ÷ sum of all counties. Some annexes are landscape tables rotated 90° on the page; these were de-rotated by word position and re-validated (maize: all 47 counties cross-check the report's Top-20 table exactly). **Crops:** maize, sorghum, finger & pearl millet, dry beans, cowpeas, green grams, pigeon peas, Irish & sweet potato. **Livestock:** cattle, sheep, goats, camels, donkeys (head, 2021). **Pending:** coffee & cotton.

produceNote.en: *Each crop is shown for the counties KNBS reports it in (county sums match the national total exactly, every year). Coffee & cotton pending.*

title.en: What Does My County Look Like?

intro.en: *County profile: the gender & equity (GESI) context and recent crop production — who a bad season puts at risk. (What the county grows is up top, under "What does my county produce?".)*

vopTitle.en: what agriculture is worth here — value of production by commodity

vopIntro.en: *The economic stakes: gross value of production by commodity, in constant international dollars (I$, purchasing-power comparable). Crops from MapSPAM 2020, livestock from GLW4 — the Atlas exposure layer. In the arid and semi-arid north and east this is overwhelmingly **livestock**, which is why a drought that fails pasture (see the NDVI chart in Block 4) hits those counties hardest.*

gesiTitle.en: gender & equity indicators (GESI, county vs Kenya)

vopCaption.en: Gross value of agricultural production by commodity, in constant international dollars (purchasing-power comparable, so counties are comparable). Crops are MapSPAM 2020, livestock GLW4 — the Atlas exposure layer, a 2020 snapshot. Green = crops, brown = livestock. Shows what a bad season puts at economic risk here.

gesiCaption.en: Gender & equity indicators for the county beside the national figure, from the KNBS County Gender Data Sheets. Each value was read by a deterministic parser and passed a 47-county consensus gate — no figure was transcribed by hand.

maizeCaption.en: Recent dry-maize production from the Agriculture & Food Authority county returns (2020–24). A short recent record, not a long climate series — the long production series lives in Block 3 (national FAOStat).

title.en: ENSO, The IOD And The Western-V: What Drives My County's Rains?

intro.en: *El Niño / La Niña is the signal you act on. But it doesn't act alone: in the **OND short rains** ENSO and the **Indian Ocean Dipole** move together (tightly coupled — see below), while the **MAM long rains** are governed mostly by a **partly-independent Western-V Pacific pattern** that ENSO explains little of. So below, county rainfall is coloured by the phase of the driver that governs each season — ENSO for OND (with the IOD marked ▲ positive / ▼ negative), the Western-V for MAM — and picking OND+MAM shows both side by side. Toggle the anomaly view to see each year's departure from normal.*

insight1.en: ENSO is the familiar trigger, but for Kenya's **OND** rains the **IOD** carries more signal (r≈0.67 vs ENSO ≈0.45) — and the two are coupled, so read them together. For the **MAM** long rains a **partly-independent Western-V** pattern matters most; **ENSO alone explains little of MAM** (Niño 3.4 ↔ Western-V r≈0.08). Switch the driver above to see it. El Niño / positive-IOD years tend wetter, La Niña / negative-IOD drier — strongest in the arid north and east.

interactIntro.en: *They are not independent levers — ENSO and the IOD are one coupled Indo-Pacific system in OND; the Western-V is a partly-separate control in MAM.*

combinedHeading.en: Combined state of all three drivers

combinedIntro.en: *Standardized (z-score) so they share one axis — read the coordinated regime at a glance.*

insight2.en: ENSO and IOD track together in OND (r ≈ 0.6) — El Niño tends to force a positive IOD, both pushing wetter short rains. The Western-V moves more independently (≈ 0 with ENSO), so it adds information ENSO alone misses for the MAM long rains. Read the combined-state chart as the ocean "regime": all three positive = strong wet signal; ENSO/IOD negative = drought risk.

calendarHeading.en: When does my county plant and harvest?

calendarIntro.en: *The crop calendar links the ocean signal to the field: **planting** follows the rains, **harvest** comes months later. Read it against the rainfall bars above — a county's long-rains (MAM) crop is planted around Mar–Apr and harvested mid-year; its short-rains (OND) crop is planted around Oct and harvested early the next year. That harvest lag is why Block 3 relates production to the season-window driver, not the calendar-year mean.*

calendarTitle.en: planting & harvest windows (JRC ASAP crop calendar)

calendarNoData.en: *No rainfed crop calendar exists for this county — it is a pastoralist (arid/semi-arid) or urban county with no main cropping season. Its seasonality is the rains themselves (the rainfall chart above) and pasture greenness — see the **vegetation condition (NDVI)** chart in Block 4, which covers all 47 counties. Crop-calendar coverage: 38 of 47 counties.*

rainCaption.en: County seasonal rainfall (CHIRPS), one bar per year, coloured by the phase of the driver that governs THAT season: the **OND** short rains by ENSO phase (El Niño / La Niña), with the **IOD** overlaid as a ▲ (positive) / ▼ (negative) marker since the two are coupled in OND; the **MAM** long rains by the **Western-V** (WNP) phase, because ENSO explains little of MAM. Selecting OND+MAM shows both panels side by side. Toggle **Anomaly** to plot each year's departure from the 1991–2020 mean instead of absolute mm.

driverCaption.en: The selected ocean driver as a per-year seasonal-mean anomaly; points coloured by ENSO phase. Switch the driver (top control) between ENSO, the IOD and the Western-V to compare what each signal was doing.

interactCaption.en: Each point is one OND season — ENSO (Niño 3.4) on the x-axis against the IOD on the y-axis — with the fitted line and the live correlation shown in the title. It shows the two behave as one coupled Indo-Pacific system in the short rains, not independent levers.

combinedCaption.en: All three drivers standardized to z-scores against the 1991–2020 reference window so they share one axis. Read it as the ocean 'regime': all positive = strong wet signal; ENSO/IOD negative = drought risk.

title.en: How Does Climate Move Kenya's Harvests?

intro.en: *⚠️ **National, not county** — Kenya has no long county-level production series yet (KNBS county data is only 2020–24), so this uses **national FAOStat**. Production is **detrended** (raw production has a strong upward trend that would swamp the climate signal) and related to the season-window driver. Staples (maize/wheat) use FAOStat; cash crops can use KNBS. **Caveat:** national maize is long-rains-dominated, so the OND/IOD signal is diluted here — the county-level short-rains signal (strongest in the arid east/north) awaits a longer county series.*

insight.en: Uses the **detrended anomaly** (production minus its long-term trend) to isolate climate-driven variability (raw maize-IOD r=0.34 is trend-inflated). **The national relationship is weak and not statistically significant** — e.g. maize vs OND-IOD r≈0.21, p≈0.09. That is expected: national maize is dominated by the *long* rains, while the IOD drives the *short* rains, and the strongest short-rains signal is a *county-level* eastern-Kenya effect this national view can't resolve. A longer county production series is needed to show it properly.

scatterCaption.en: National detrended production anomaly against the season-window driver, with the live correlation, sample size and significance in the title. The regression line is solid if significant, dashed and faint if not — so a weak relationship is not dressed up as a signal. National FAOStat, not county.

trendCaption.en: The production series (blue) and its fitted linear trend (dashed) — what is removed to make the detrended anomaly in the scatter above. FAOStat, 1961–present.

title.en: How Does A Bad Season Reach People?

intro.en: *Food insecurity (IPC), conflict, and market prices, for the selected county.*

pricesIntro.en: *Monthly retail prices in the county's monitored markets (FEWS NET FDW; the axis shows KES per the unit the product is traded in). Price spikes often follow failed seasons — read alongside the IPC line above.*

pricesNoData.en: *No FEWS NET market price series is available for this county (coverage: 42 of 47 counties).*

rwIntro.en: *County-tagged humanitarian reports from ReliefWeb (2010–present). A report tagged with several hazards counts once, under its first match: drought → flood → epidemic → other. Titles below link to the source documents.*

ndviTitle.en: vegetation condition — NDVI vs the long-term normal

ndviIntro.en: *The clearest bridge from a failed rain season to people — especially in the pastoralist ASAL, where livelihoods ride on pasture, not crops. The line is dekadal (10-day) NDVI as a **percentage of that dekad's long-term normal**: below 100 (orange) = vegetation deficit / drought stress, above 100 (green) = greener than usual. MODIS via WFP VAM, 2002–present, aggregated to the county. Watch the deep, sustained deficits — 2011, 2017 and 2021–22 are Kenya's major droughts.*

tradeIntro.en: *⚠️ **National, not your county** — cross-border trade is measured at national border points, so this is a country-level supply layer, the same for every county. It matters because Kenya is a structural **maize-deficit importer** (Uganda, Tanzania) and the ASAL pastoralist economy runs on **cross-border livestock** trade (Ethiopia, Somalia). When a drought hits, import reliance and prices rise together — read this beside the market-price and NDVI charts above. FEWS NET XBT, 2010–2024; informal flows are field estimates.*

mapNote.en: *Arrow width = total traded quantity over the record; orange = imports into Kenya, green = exports from Kenya. Flows are drawn between country centres, not exact border crossings.*

importsTitle.en: imports into Kenya, by partner (per year)

ipcCaption.en: IPC food-insecurity phase for the county (worst-area, Current Situation), from FEWS NET. Phase 3 (the dashed line) is Crisis; higher is worse.

acledCaption.en: Conflict fatalities per year for the county, from ACLED. Context for the impacts pathway; the climate–conflict link is exploratory (small sample) and is never presented as a headline figure.

pricesCaption.en: Monthly retail price in the county's monitored markets (FEWS NET FDW), one line per market. Only retail is shown so the axis unit stays consistent per product. Price spikes often follow failed seasons — read it beside the IPC line above.

rwCaption.en: County-tagged humanitarian reports per year from ReliefWeb (2010–present), stacked by hazard. A report tagged with several hazards is counted once, under its first match (drought → flood → epidemic → other). The table lists the most recent reports with links to the source documents.

ndviCaption.en: Dekadal NDVI as a percentage of that dekad's long-term normal (MODIS via WFP VAM, pixel-weighted to the county). Below 100 (orange) = vegetation deficit / drought stress; above 100 (green) = greener than usual. The clearest bridge from a failed rain season to pasture and people.

mapCaptionXbt.en: National cross-border trade for the selected product (FEWS NET XBT, 2010–2024). Arrows run between country centres — orange into Kenya (imports), green out (exports) — with width scaled by total traded quantity. National / border-point data, the same for every county.

importsCaption.en: Imports into Kenya per year by partner country for the selected product (FEWS NET XBT). Grounds Kenya's structural maize deficit (Uganda, Tanzania) and the ASAL cross-border livestock trade (Ethiopia).

title.en: Where Are We Now, What's Coming?

intro.en: *Recent state of the three ocean drivers. ENSO is the signal to act on; the IOD leads the OND short rains; the Western-V is a partly-independent control on the MAM long rains.*

watch.en: **What to watch.** OND short-rains outlook is skilfully forecastable (IOD); MAM long rains are not. For the live forecast see the [NOAA CPC ENSO advisory](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/analysis_monitoring/enso_advisory/ensodisc.shtml) and [FEWS NET East Africa seasonal monitor](https://fews.net/east-africa).

recentCaption.en: The three ocean drivers over recent years on one axis: Niño 3.4 (°C), the IOD DMI (HadISST coalesced with ERSST to reach the present), and the Western-V (WNP z-score). The forecast context for the outlook.

text.en: Drivers: NOAA ONI/Niño 3.4 + HadISST DMI + Western-V/WNP computed from ERSSTv5 (Funk et al. 2018 boxes; Niño 3.4 validated r=0.998 vs NOAA, WNP reproduces Funk's post-1997 MAM sign). Rainfall: CHIRPS v3 (Atlas hub, county). Production: FAOStat (physical, staples) + KNBS Statistical Abstract (marketed value/volume, dual-engine validated) + AFA/NAPR (county recent). GESI: KNBS County Gender Data Sheets (47-way Kenya-benchmark consensus). Impacts: FEWS NET IPC + ACLED conflict + FEWS NET FDW market prices (retail, county markets) + ReliefWeb county-tagged humanitarian reports (API, first live run 2026-07-09) + vegetation condition (NDVI as % of the 2002+ dekadal normal, MODIS 6.1 via WFP VAM, pixel-weighted to county). Cross-border trade (Block 4, national context): FEWS NET East Africa Cross-Border Trade (XBT) monitoring, 2010–2024 — national/border-point resolution (not county); informal flows are field aggregations. **Detrending (Block 3):** production series are linearly detrended per crop before relating to climate drivers — the driver indices are stationary anomalies, so raw levels would be trend-confounded (e.g. maize-IOD raw r=0.34 vs detrended r=0.21). Block 3 uses the residual anomaly. Full catalog + provenance: `_master/DATA_CATALOG.md` (D409 project store). Every value validated by an LLM-independent gate (dual-engine / additivity / cross-edition / consensus); no numbers transcribed by AI. See `METHODOLOGY_extraction_QA.md`.
